title: Al Zubarah founded
description: Utub merchants from Kuwait built a walled pearling town on the northwest coast that grew into the Gulf's busiest entrepôt before it was destroyed.

title: War with Bahrain
description: Bahraini and Abu Dhabi forces sacked Doha and Al Wakrah in a campaign against the Al Thani, opening the feud that forced Britain to deal with Qatar's rulers directly.

title: First treaty with Britain
description: Muhammad bin Thani signed a maritime truce with Britain, treating the Al Thani for the first time as the independent rulers of Qatar.

title: Sheikh Jassim consolidates power
description: On his father's retirement Jassim bin Muhammad became the effective ruler, honoured in Qatar as the founder of the modern state.

title: Battle of Al Wajbah
description: Sheikh Jassim's Qataris defeated the Ottoman expedition from Basra, a victory that secured de facto independence and gave Qatar a founding national story.

title: Anglo-Qatari treaty
description: Britain recognised Sheikh Abdullah bin Jassim and promised protection, bringing Qatar into the trucial system and out of the Ottoman orbit.

title: Oil found at Dukhan
description: Drillers struck oil on the west coast just as pearl diving collapsed, though exports only began after the war.

title: First oil export
description: Qatar's first shipment of crude marked the beginning of the oil income that transformed the decade after.

title: First constitution
description: A provisional constitution and a first cabinet were put in place as Britain prepared to leave the Gulf.

title: Independence
description: Qatar ended its treaties with Britain and declared independence under Emir Ahmad bin Ali, choosing, like Bahrain, to stay out of the new United Arab Emirates.

title: Khalifa bin Hamad takes power
description: The deputy emir, already running the country, took power from his cousin without violence and ruled for twenty-three years.

title: Hamad takes power
description: Emir Hamad deposed his father while he was abroad, opening an era of gas money, bold diplomacy and Al Jazeera.

title: Al Jazeera founded
description: The emir launched a satellite news channel whose free-wheeling Arabic broadcasts broke state monopolies and made Qatar famous.

title: First LNG plant at Ras Laffan
description: The first liquefied natural gas plant at Ras Laffan was commissioned, beginning Qatar's rise to become the world's leading LNG exporter.

title: Women vote in municipal elections
description: In the first elections to the Central Municipal Council women voted and stood as candidates, a first in the Gulf.

title: Permanent constitution approved
description: Voters overwhelmingly approved the permanent constitution, which came into force in 2004 and promised a partly elected advisory council.

title: Museum of Islamic Art opens
description: I. M. Pei's museum on the Corniche opened, the showpiece of Qatar's investment in culture.

title: 2022 World Cup awarded
description: FIFA chose Qatar to host the 2022 World Cup, beating bids from the United States, Australia, Japan and South Korea.

title: Tamim becomes emir
description: Hamad handed power to his 33-year-old son Tamim, a rare voluntary abdication in the region.

title: Gulf crisis
description: Saudi Arabia, the Emirates, Bahrain and Egypt cut ties and closed Qatar's land border and air routes, a blockade Qatar weathered by deepening links with Turkey and Iran.
